findings.fix: Delete the six lemmas. `gaPointsMulEquiv_gaPointMul` (line 227), which the PR already adds, plus `MulEquiv.injective` reduces any such identity to the `A`-side axiom in one line at the call site (e.g. `apply gaPointsMulEquiv.injective; simp [mul_comm]`). Keep `gaPointMul`, `gaPointsMulEquiv_gaPointMul`, `gaPointMul_apply_ι` and `mapValue_gaPointMul`, which have consumers or state genuine naturality.
findings.issue: `gaPointMul_one_left` (259), `gaPointMul_one_right` (267), `gaPointMul_comm` (273), `gaPointMul_assoc` (280), `gaPointMul_mul_left` (288) and `gaPointMul_mul_right` (299) are transports of `zero_mul`, `mul_zero`, `mul_comm`, `mul_assoc`, `add_mul`, `mul_add` on `A` across the equivalence `gaPointsMulEquiv`, a parallel copy of `A`'s existing `CommSemiring` API on the points type. Each proof body is literally `(gaPointsMulEquiv).injective` plus the corresponding `A`-axiom, and none of the six is used anywhere: `grep -rn "gaPointMul" TauCeti` shows uses only of `gaPointMul_apply_ι` and `gaPointsMulEquiv_gaPointMul` (in `GeneralLinear/ChevalleyRelations.lean:91,98`); all six appear solely at their own declarations.

summary: The transported root-subgroup relations and the `gaPointMul` core (definition, transport lemma, `_apply_ι`, naturality) are genuinely new and reuse the existing transvection API correctly. The six algebraic-law lemmas on `gaPointMul` are a parallel restatement of `A`'s commutative-semiring axioms through `gaPointsMulEquiv`, with no consumer.
